mainTopic: When a father or husband is believed about a woman's status: a father about his daughter's קידושין and captivity, and a dying man about having children or brothers.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier ruling: a father is believed about his child's age for נדרים, חרמים, הקדשות and ערכים, but not for מלקות or other punishments. A new משנה then teaches that a father is believed that he was מקדש his daughter, or that she was divorced, while she is still a קטנה. He is not believed once she is a גדולה, and he is never believed that she was taken captive. The גמרא first explains this by saying he is believed about what is in his power (בידו). It defends that idea through a series of challenges involving a חלל, a ממזר and a widow married to a כהן גדול, using the views of רבי עקיבא, רבי סימאי and רבי ישבב. רב אשי then rejects the בידו approach, since a father cannot divorce his daughter or force a groom on his own. Instead he teaches that the Torah itself trusts a father about his daughter's marriage, learned from "את בתי נתתי לאיש הזה", but not about captivity. A second משנה rules that a dying man is believed when he says "I have children" but not when he says "I have brothers." The גמרא asks whether this argues with רבי נתן; after רבא's answer is challenged, אביי explains that the משנה deals with a case where nothing is known about his family, and he begins to explain the ברייתא's case, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Father believed about his child's age for vows, not for punishments
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier ruling. A father's word about his child's age counts for נדרים, חרמים, הקדשות and ערכים, but not for מלקות or other punishments.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is believed regarding vows, dedications, consecrations, and valuations, but not regarding lashes and punishments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ruling from the page before: a father who states his child's age is believed in some areas but not in others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the father says the child is old enough, the child's נדרים, חרמים, הקדשות and ערכים take effect based on his word. But no one may receive מלקות or another punishment on his word alone. Punishment needs full proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Items dedicated with the word חרם
Items made holy for the בית המקדש
Fixed-value pledges of a person's worth to the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: A father's word about his child's age can make vows take effect, but it can never be the basis for punishing the child.

phrases.english: He is believed regarding vows,
phrases.notes: "He" is the father, who is telling us his child's age. This line finishes a ruling from the page before.

phrases.english: and regarding dedications, consecrations, and valuations,
but not regarding lashes and punishments.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱמָן לִנְדָרִים, וְלַחֲרָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ruling from the previous page about a father stating his child's age.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father's word about his child's age counts for נדרים, חרמים, הקדשות and ערכים, but not for מלקות and punishments.

steps.title: Father's claim of betrothing or divorcing his daughter: minor versus adult
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: a father is believed that he was מקדש his daughter, or was מקדש her and she was divorced while a קטנה, if she is still a קטנה now. If she is now a גדולה, he is not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a father says, 'I betrothed my daughter,' or 'I betrothed her and received her divorce when she was a minor,' and she is still a minor, he is believed. If he says, 'I betrothed her and received her divorce when she was a minor,' but she is now an adult, he is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on when a father is believed about his daughter's קידושין and גירושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he is believed, she becomes an אשת איש, or a גרושה who is forbidden to a כהן. While she is a קטנה, his word counts. Once she is a גדולה, the exact same claim about the past is no longer accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor girl, under her father's control
An adult woman, no longer under her father's control for marriage

steps.confusionAlert: In both the believed case and the not-believed case, the father says the events happened while she was a קטנה. The only difference is how old she is NOW, when he says it.

phrases.english: MISHNA: 'I betrothed my daughter,'
'I betrothed her and received her divorce when she was a minor,'
and she is still a minor — he is believed.
'I betrothed her and received her divorce when she was a minor,'
and she is now an adult — he is not believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ ״קִדַּשְׁתִּי אֶת בִּתִּי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father is believed about his daughter's קידושין and גירושין only while she is still a קטנה.

steps.title: Father's claim that his daughter was taken captive
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: if a father says his daughter was taken captive and he redeemed her, he is not believed, whether she is a קטנה or a גדולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says, 'She was taken captive and I redeemed her,' he is not believed, whether she is a minor or an adult.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more case: a father's claim that his daughter was a captive. Here he is never believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a captive would make her forbidden to a כהן. Unlike the קידושין case, her age makes no difference here. He is not believed even while she is a קטנה.

keyTerms.meaning: I redeemed her (paid to free her)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives three outcomes: about קידושין and גירושין he is believed while she is a קטנה, not once she is a גדולה, and about captivity he is never believed.

phrases.english: 'She was taken captive and I redeemed her,'
phrases.notes: A woman who was held captive is treated as possibly violated, so she may not marry a כהן.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁהִיא קְטַנָּה בֵּין שֶׁהִיא גְּדוֹלָה –
phrases.english: whether she is a minor or an adult —
he is not believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִשְׁבֵּית וּפְדִיתִיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a different kind of claim.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father is never believed that his daughter was taken captive.

steps.title: Why are the cases in the משנה different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the father is believed in the first case but not in the later ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: What is different about the first clause, and what is different about the later clause?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the משנה's different rulings. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In every case, the father makes a claim that hurts his daughter's status. So why is he believed when she is a קטנה, but not when she is a גדולה or about captivity? The גמרא is looking for the rule that explains the split.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה
The later part of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is different about the first clause,
phrases.notes: The first clause is the case where she is still a קטנה.

phrases.english: and what is different about the later clause?
phrases.notes: The later clause covers both the case where she is now a גדולה and the captivity case.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the משנה's rulings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle explains why the father is believed in some cases and not in others?

steps.title: He is believed about what is in his power
steps.stepSummary: Answer: in the first case, doing this is still in his power (בידו). In the later cases, it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the first clause, it is in his power. In the later clause, it is not in his power.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The father is believed only about things he could do right now anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While she is a קטנה, a father can be מקדש her, so his claim that he did it already is believed. Once she is a גדולה, he can no longer be מקדש her. He also has no power to make her a captive. So in those cases his word is not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: In his power (he could do it now)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule of בידו: a person is believed about something he has the power to do right now. The next step tests this rule.

phrases.english: The first clause: it is in his power;
the later clause: it is not in his power.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא בִּידֵיהּ, סֵיפָא לָאו בִּידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The father is believed only where the act is still in his power (בידו).

steps.title: But he can marry her to a חלל
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: a father does have the power to make his daughter unfit for כהונה, by marrying her to a חלל. So he should be believed about captivity too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it not in his power? But it is in his power to marry her to a חלל, which disqualifies her from the priesthood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave, as it applies to the captivity case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The result of captivity is that she becomes unfit to marry a כהן. A father can bring about that same result himself, by marrying his young daughter to a חלל. So by the rule of בידו, he should be believed when he says she was captured.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of a כהן from a forbidden marriage; he does not have the status of a כהן
Makes her unfit to marry a כהן

phrases.english: And is it not (in his power)?
But it is in his power to marry her to a חלל,
which disqualifies her from the priesthood!
phrases.notes: A woman who has relations with a חלל can no longer marry a כהן. That is the same result captivity would cause.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא? וַהֲרֵי בְּיָדוֹ לְהַשִּׂיאָהּ לְחָלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 5 as it applies to the captivity case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that making her unfit for כהונה through captivity is 'not in his power.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The father can bring about the same result himself by marrying her to a חלל. So the result is in his power, and by the rule of בידו he should be believed about captivity.

steps.title: Marrying her to a חלל does not make her unfit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה, who holds that a Jewish woman who marries a חלל stays fit, so the father has no power to make her unfit this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. The משנה follows רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה, who says: Jewish daughters are like a pure מקוה for חללים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 6. Marrying a חלל does not ruin the daughter for כהונה, according to רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said the father can make her unfit by marrying her to a חלל. רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה says a regular Jewish woman stays fit even after marrying a חלל, and her daughters are fit too. So this is not actually in the father's power, and the rule of בידו still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult; the challenge has an answer
A pure מקוה; here a picture for keeping something fit
Men born from a forbidden כהן marriage, who lost כהונה status

phrases.english: This is not difficult,
it follows Rabbi Dostai ben Yehuda, who says:
Jewish daughters are a pure ritual bath for חללים.
phrases.notes: Just like a מקוה makes things pure, a Jewish woman keeps her family fit even when married to a חלל.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, כְּרַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בֶּן יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a specific תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father can make her unfit by marrying her to a חלל
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה, a woman married to a חלל stays fit, so the father has no such power

steps.title: But he can marry her to a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: the father could marry his daughter to a ממזר and make her unfit for כהונה that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is in his power to marry her to a ממזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new way the father seems able to make his daughter unfit: marrying her to a ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי דוסתאי's rule only covers a חלל. Marrying a ממזר is a forbidden union, and that would make her unfit for כהונה. So the father seems to have the power again.

keyTerms.meaning: A child from a forbidden union, who may not marry a regular Jew

phrases.english: But it is in his power to marry her to a ממזר!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי בְּיָדוֹ לְהַשִּׂיאָהּ לְמַמְזֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New challenge after Step 7's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the father has no power to make her unfit (Steps 5 and 7)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Marrying her to a ממזר would make her unfit for כהונה, and the father can do that

steps.title: The marriage to a ממזר does not take effect
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who holds that קידושין do not take effect when the union is forbidden by a לאו, so the father cannot marry her to a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבי עקיבא, who says: קידושין do not take effect with those forbidden by a לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by saying the משנה follows רבי עקיבא. His view means the father simply cannot marry her to a ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ממזר marrying a Jewish woman is forbidden by a לאו. רבי עקיבא holds that קידושין don't work at all in such cases. Since the father's power is through making קידושין, he has no way to do this.

keyTerms.meaning: The first step of Jewish marriage, which makes her a married woman
Unions forbidden by a simple negative commandment (a לאו)

phrases.english: It follows Rabbi Akiva, who says:
Betrothal does not take effect with those forbidden by a לאו.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a specific תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father can marry her to a ממזר and make her unfit
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי עקיבא, such קידושין do not take effect, so the father cannot do it

steps.title: But he can marry her, as a widow, to a כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: according to רבי סימאי, רבי עקיבא agrees that a widow's marriage to a כהן גדול does take effect, so the father can make her unfit that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is in his power to marry her, as a widow, to a כהן גדול. This fits רבי סימאי, who taught: רבי עקיבא makes a ממזר from every forbidden union except a widow with a כהן גדול, because the תורה says 'he shall not take... and he shall not profane.' That union makes חללים, not ממזרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another case even within רבי עקיבא's view: a widow marrying a כהן גדול. It quotes רבי סימאי to show that this marriage does take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said רבי עקיבא's rule blocks marriages forbidden by a לאו. But רבי סימאי says רבי עקיבא made an exception for a widow and a כהן גדול: the פסוק calls the children חללים, not ממזרים, so the marriage works. If so, the father could marry his widowed daughter to a כהן גדול and she becomes unfit for כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow marrying a כהן גדול, which the תורה forbids
As was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: רבי סימאי is not arguing on רבי עקיבא; he is telling us how he understands רבי עקיבא. Step 11 will bring a different understanding of the same רבי עקיבא.

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי בְּיָדוֹ לְהַשִּׂיאָהּ אַלְמָנָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: But it is in his power to marry her, as a widow, to a כהן גדול,
and this follows Rabbi Simai, as was taught:
Rabbi Simai says:

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַכֹּל עוֹשֶׂה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַמְזֵר,
phrases.english: From every forbidden union Rabbi Akiva makes the child a ממזר,
except for a widow with a כהן גדול,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה: ״לֹא יִקָּח... וְלֹא יְחַלֵּל״: –
phrases.english: for the Torah says: 'He shall not take... and he shall not profane':
he makes חללים, but he does not make ממזרים.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי בְּיָדוֹ לְהַשִּׂיאָהּ אַלְמָנָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New challenge against Step 9's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that under רבי עקיבא the father has no power to make her unfit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי סימאי says רבי עקיבא lets a widow's marriage to a כהן גדול take effect, so the father can make her a חללה

steps.title: רבי ישבב: for רבי עקיבא, every forbidden union makes a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי ישבב's understanding of רבי עקיבא: every forbidden union produces a ממזר, so even a widow's marriage to a כהן גדול does not take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבי ישבב, who said: Come, let us cry out against עקיבא בן יוסף, who used to say that in any union a Jew is forbidden to have, the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by bringing רבי ישבב's version of רבי עקיבא. In his version, there is no exception for a widow and a כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישבב understood רבי עקיבא as saying every forbidden union makes a ממזר, with no exceptions. So the marriage of a widow to a כהן גדול does not take effect either. That means the father truly has no way to make her unfit for כהונה, and he is not believed about her captivity.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us cry out, protest loudly

steps.whatToRemember: Under רבי עקיבא as רבי ישבב understands him, a father cannot make his daughter unfit for כהונה by any marriage forbidden by a לאו. The next step asks whether unions forbidden by an עשה still leave him that power, and in Step 13 רב אשי drops the בידו approach altogether.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the challenge from Step 10 for now. Step 12 questions whether רבי ישבב's view really reaches this far, and in Step 13 רב אשי rejects the בידו approach altogether.

phrases.english: It follows Rabbi Yeshevav, who said:

phrases.aramaic: בּוֹאוּ וְנִצְוַוח עַל עֲקִיבָא בֶּן יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: Come, let us cry out against Akiva ben Yosef,
phrases.notes: This is רבי עקיבא, called here by his father's name.

phrases.english: who used to say:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בִּיאָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הַוָּלָד מַמְזֵר.
phrases.english: Any union a Jew is not permitted to have, the child is a ממזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי יְשֵׁבָב, דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Choosing a different understanding of the same תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא allows a widow's marriage to a כהן גדול to take effect, as רבי סימאי said
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי ישבב, רבי עקיבא holds every forbidden union makes a ממזר, so no such marriage works and the father has no power

steps.title: Even רבי ישבב might leave a gap: marrying her to someone forbidden by a positive commandment
steps.stepSummary: The answer from רבי ישבב only works if he made a general statement. If he was only arguing with רבי סימאי about a לאו, then a marriage forbidden only by an עשה would still take effect, and the father keeps his power.
steps.simpleTranslation: That works for רבי ישבב if he was stating his own general view. But if he only came to argue with רבי סימאי's reasoning, then the father could still marry her to someone forbidden to her by a positive commandment!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer from step 11. It asks how far רבי ישבב's view really reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישבב might be saying that every forbidden union creates a ממזר, which would block every case. Or he might only be disagreeing with רבי סימאי about the widow and כהן גדול, which is a לאו. In that second reading, unions forbidden only by an עשה would still be valid קידושין, so the father would still have power over her status, and the בידו explanation fails again.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (opens a 'fine for X, but what about Y' challenge)
Unions forbidden by a positive commandment (an עשה), not by a לאו

phrases.english: This works out well according to Rabbi Yeshevav
if he is stating his own reasoning, that is fine.
phrases.notes: He means that רבי ישבב made his own general statement covering every forbidden union.

phrases.english: But if he comes to exclude
the reasoning of Rabbi Simai,
then it is in his power to marry her to those forbidden by a positive commandment!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי יְשֵׁבָב אִי לְטַעְמֵיהּ דְּנַפְשֵׁיהּ שַׁפִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the answer in step 11 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה follows רבי ישבב's reading of רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי ישבב only argued with רבי סימאי about a לאו case, then unions forbidden by an עשה still take effect. So the father still has power, and the בידו reasoning would require him to be believed about captivity too.

steps.title: רב אשי rejects the idea that the father is believed because it is in his power
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי attacks the starting assumption behind the whole line of reasoning. A father cannot divorce his daughter on his own, and he cannot force a man to marry her, so his 'power' cannot be the reason he is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Do you really think the first part of the משנה is because it is in his power? Granted, he can betroth her, but can he divorce her? And also, if the man says he does not want her, can the father betroth her to him against his will?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי steps back and rejects the basic idea the גמרא has been defending since the first answer about בידו. This clears the way for his own explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה believes the father when he says "I betrothed her and divorced her." A divorce depends on the husband giving a גט, so it is not in the father's power. Even betrothal needs a willing groom. So בידו cannot explain the רישא, and all the back-and-forth about ways to make her unfit no longer matters.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? (opens a rejection)
The first clause of the משנה
In his power, he is able to do it now

steps.whatToRemember: The בידו approach fails because a father can neither divorce his daughter on his own nor force a man to marry her.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: And can you really think so?
Is the first clause because it is in his power?
Granted it is in his power to betroth her,
is it in his power to divorce her?
phrases.notes: The משנה believes him when he says he betrothed her and she was divorced. A divorce comes from the husband, not the father.

phrases.english: And furthermore, if this man said
that he is not pleased with her,
phrases.notes: Some versions add the words in square brackets here.

phrases.aramaic: מִי מָצֵי מְקַדֵּשׁ [לַהּ] נִיהֲלֵיהּ בְּעַל כֻּרְחֵיהּ?
phrases.english: could he betroth her to him against his will?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי וְתִסְבְּרַאּ רֵישָׁא מִשּׁוּם דִּבְיָדוֹ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Instead of answering step 12, rejects the assumption behind the whole line of reasoning.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole explanation that the father is believed in the רישא because of בידו
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The father has no power to divorce his daughter, and he cannot force a groom, so his power cannot be the reason he is believed.

steps.title: The Torah itself believes the father, as רב הונא taught from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the father is believed in the רישא because the Torah gives him that trust. רב הונא in the name of רב learns this from "את בתי נתתי לאיש הזה".
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: In the first clause, the Torah believed him. This follows רב הונא, who said in the name of רב: How do we know a father is believed by Torah law to make his daughter forbidden? Because it says, "I gave my daughter to this man." "To the man" — he made her forbidden. "This" — he made her permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new reason for the רישא. The father's word is trusted because the Torah says so, not because of his power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the father's words alone establish that his daughter is married. "לאיש" makes her forbidden to every man, and "הזה" makes her permitted to this one husband. So the Torah gives a father special believability about his daughter's marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah (the Merciful One) believed him

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the basis of the משנה from what the father can do to what the Torah trusts him to say. That is what allows the משנה to tell marriage apart from captivity.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
In the first clause, the Merciful One believed him,
in line with Rav Huna,
as Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
From where do we know that a father is believed
to make his daughter forbidden by Torah law?
As it is said: "I gave my daughter to this man,"
"to the man" — he made her forbidden,
"this" — he made her permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי רֵישָׁא רַחֲמָנָא הֵימְנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting בידו, רב אשי gives a new reason for the רישא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the reasoning: Torah-given trust instead of the father's power
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father is believed because it is in his power to marry her off.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father is believed because the Torah trusts him about his daughter's marriage (רב הונא from דברים 22:16).

steps.title: The father is trusted about marriage, not about captivity
steps.stepSummary: The Torah's trust in the father covers only his daughter's marriage. It does not cover a claim that she was taken captive.
steps.simpleTranslation: About marriage, the Torah believed the father. About a captive, it did not believe him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses רב אשי's reason to explain the משנה's סיפא. The father is not believed when he says "she was captured and I redeemed her."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The special trust comes from a פסוק about marriage, so it reaches only as far as marriage. Captivity is a different topic. There the father is like anyone else, so he is not believed, whether she is a minor or an adult.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's rule: the Torah believes a father about his daughter's marriage, but not about her being taken captive. That is why the רישא and סיפא of the משנה differ.

phrases.english: Regarding marriage, the Merciful One believed the father,
regarding a captive, He did not believe him.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנִישּׂוּאִין הֵימְנֵיהּ רַחֲמָנָא לְאָב בִּשְׁבוּיָיה לָא הֵימְנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב אשי's reason to explain the difference between the רישא and the סיפא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The father's believability is a Torah-given trust limited to marriage. So he is believed about betrothing his daughter, but not about her having been taken captive.

steps.title: משנה: a dying man saying he has children or brothers
steps.stepSummary: A man on his deathbed is believed when he says "I have children." He is not believed when he says "I have brothers."
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man says at the time of his death, "I have children," he is believed. If he says, "I have brothers," he is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives two rulings about what a dying man says regarding his family. One claim is accepted and the other is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a man dies with children, his wife needs no יבום or חליצה and may marry anyone. If he dies childless and has brothers, she is tied to them until יבום or חליצה. "I have children" frees her, so he is believed. "I have brothers" ties her down, so he is not believed.

keyTerms.meaning: at the time of his death, on his deathbed
levirate marriage, where a brother marries the widow of a man who died childless
the ceremony that releases a widow from יבום

phrases.english: MISHNAH
One who said at the time of his death
"I have children" – he is believed.
phrases.notes: Having children means his wife will not need יבום, so she is free to marry anyone.

phrases.english: "I have brothers" – he is not believed.
phrases.notes: This claim would tie her to his brothers for יבום or חליצה, which forbids her to anyone else.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁאָמַר בִּשְׁעַת מִיתָתוֹ יֵשׁ לִי בָּנִים נֶאֱמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic after the father-and-daughter discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dying man is believed when he says "I have children" but not when he says "I have brothers."

steps.title: Inference: believed to permit, not to forbid, so maybe against רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws a rule from the משנה: a husband is believed to permit his wife but not to forbid her. It then asks whether this means the משנה argues with רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Apparently he is believed to permit but not believed to forbid. Shall we say our משנה does not follow רבי נתן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls a general rule out of the משנה. It then raises the possibility that the משנה disagrees with רבי נתן, and this sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rulings in the משנה fit one pattern: claims that free the wife are accepted, and claims that tie her down are rejected. The גמרא tests this pattern against a known opinion, רבי נתן's, which believes the husband even to forbid.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Apparently, he is believed to permit
but he is not believed to forbid.
Shall we say our Mishnah is not in line with Rabbi Natan?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא נֶאֱמָן לְהַתִּיר וְאֵין נֶאֱמָן לֶאֱסוֹר נֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from the משנה and asks which תנא it follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the משנה disagree with רבי נתן, who believes a husband even to forbid?

steps.title: The ברייתא where רבי and רבי נתן argue
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי believes the husband only to permit, while רבי נתן believes him even to forbid.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: Suppose a man said at his betrothal that he has children, and at his death he said he has none. Or suppose he said at his betrothal that he has no brothers, and at his death he said he has brothers. רבי says he is believed to permit but not to forbid. רבי נתן says he is believed even to forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that is the source for רבי נתן's view. This explains why it suggested that the משנה disagrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the husband's first statement frees his wife and his deathbed statement ties her to יבום. רבי follows the statement that frees her. רבי נתן accepts even the later statement that forbids her. That seems to clash with the משנה's rule that he is not believed to forbid.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא
the words of רבי יהודה הנשיא

steps.confusionAlert: In both cases of the ברייתא, "permit" means following his first statement, made at betrothal. "Forbid" means following his later statement, made at death. Do not mix up which statement frees her.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁעַת קִידּוּשִׁין אָמַר יֵשׁ לוֹ בָּנִים,
phrases.english: At the time of betrothal he said he has children,

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁעַת מִיתָה אָמַר אֵין לוֹ בָּנִים,
phrases.english: at the time of death he said he has no children;

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁעַת קִידּוּשִׁין אָמַר אֵין לוֹ אַחִים,
phrases.english: at the time of betrothal he said he has no brothers,

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁעַת מִיתָה אָמַר יֵשׁ לוֹ אַחִים –
phrases.english: at the time of death he said he has brothers –
he is believed to permit and not believed to forbid,
these are the words of Rebbi.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: אַף נֶאֱמָן לֶאֱסוֹר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says: he is believed even to forbid.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא בִּשְׁעַת קִידּוּשִׁין אָמַר יֵשׁ לוֹ בָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the suggestion in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי נתן believes a husband even to forbid, which seems to clash with the משנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא recording the argument between רבי and רבי נתן

steps.title: רבא: רבי נתן's case is special because the man retracted
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי נתן believes the husband only because he changed his story at death, which suggests he is now telling the truth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is different there. Since he went back on his words at the time of death, we say he is telling the truth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries to show that the משנה can agree with רבי נתן after all. He limits רבי נתן's view to a man who reversed himself on his deathbed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A deathbed reversal makes the new claim believable, as if he is setting the record straight before he dies. In the משנה there is no reversal, so even רבי נתן might agree that he is not believed to forbid.

keyTerms.meaning: he retracted, went back on his words

phrases.english: Rava said: It is different there,
phrases.notes: "There" means the ברייתא, where רבי נתן believed him to forbid.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּבִשְׁעַת מִיתָה קָא הָדַר בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: since at the time of death he goes back on his words,
we can say he is telling the truth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא שָׁאנֵי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion that the משנה disagrees with רבי נתן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a deathbed reversal versus a single statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה disagrees with רבי נתן, who believes a husband to forbid.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי נתן believes him only when he reverses himself at death. In the משנה's case, with no reversal, he may agree that the husband is not believed.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה's case should be believed even more
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues with a קל וחומר. If a man who contradicts himself is believed, then a man who never contradicted himself should be believed all the more.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Isn't that all the more reason? There, he weakens his own earlier words, and still you say he is telling the truth. In our משנה, where he does not weaken his words, all the more so he should be believed!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's answer. He argues that the difference רבא pointed to actually makes the משנה's case stronger, not weaker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Contradicting yourself normally hurts your believability, yet in the ברייתא he is still believed. The man in the משנה made only one statement with nothing against it. So by רבי נתן's logic he should certainly be believed, and the משנה still seems to disagree with רבי נתן.

keyTerms.meaning: an argument from a weaker case to a stronger one

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Isn't it all the more so?
Now, if there,
where he weakens his own statement,
you say he is telling the truth,

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִיתִין, דְּלָא קָא מַרַע לֵיהּ לְדִבּוּרֵיהּ,
phrases.english: in our Mishnah, where he does not weaken his statement,
is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי וְלָאו כָּל דְּכֵן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's distinction that רבי נתן believes the husband only because he retracted at death
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: a self-contradicting statement is weaker than a single statement. If רבי נתן believes the weaker one, he must believe the stronger one, so the משנה still disagrees with him.

steps.title: אביי places the משנה in a case where nothing is known about children or brothers
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the משנה deals with a case where the court has no prior knowledge of the man's children or brothers. There, he is believed to permit his wife but not to forbid her to everyone. The ברייתא, he begins to say, is about a different case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: The משנה is talking about a case where we have no known status about his brothers and no known status about his children. Since we know nothing either way, if he says 'I have children,' he is believed. If he says 'I have brothers,' he is not believed, because it is not in his power to forbid her to everyone. The ברייתא, however, is talking about...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי sets aside רבא's answer and gives his own: the משנה is about a man whose family situation is unknown to the court. The last word, 'ברייתא', sets up the next move, where the גמרא explains which case the ברייתא is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When nothing is known about children or brothers, the wife's starting status is permitted to marry anyone. Saying 'I have children' keeps her permitted, so he is believed. Saying 'I have brothers' would tie her to his brothers and forbid her to everyone else, and he cannot change her status that way on his word alone.

keyTerms.meaning: We have a known status, meaning the court already knows the facts
It is not in his power, so his word alone cannot do this

steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not say a dying man is never believed about brothers. He is not believed here only because the court has no information, so her default status is permitted and his claim would make it stricter.
steps.whyThisMatters: With this answer the משנה and the ברייתא are about different cases, so the משנה no longer has to argue with רבי נתן.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
Our mishna is where we have no known status about brothers
and we have no known status about children,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמְרִינַן: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא מוּחְזָק לַן בִּבְנֵי
phrases.english: as we say: Since we have no known status about children
nor about brothers,
if he said 'I have children,' he is believed;
'I have brothers,' he is not believed.
It is not in his power
to forbid her to everyone.
The baraita...

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבא's answer with a קל וחומר, אביי offers a new way to reconcile the משנה with רבי נתן by defining the משנה's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction: the משנה and the ברייתא are about different factual situations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's rule (believed to permit, not to forbid) seemed to argue with רבי נתן, who believes the husband even to forbid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a case with no known status about children or brothers, where the default is that she is permitted. The ברייתא is about a different case, explained next.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When nothing is known, a dying man is believed to say 'I have children' but not 'I have brothers,' since he cannot forbid her to everyone.
